title: Why Ford Built a Mustang to Beat Porsche

scenes.text: Why did Ford build a Mustang to beat Porsche? Here is the honest answer, and it starts with a correction. None of the sources we read says Ford built the Mustang GTD to beat Porsche. What they do say is stranger and more specific: a Le Mans race car, a chief executive who liked it, a seven-minute lap of the Nürburgring, and a Canadian company called Multimatic. This is the story, with every claim sourced.
scenes.caption: WHY FORD BUILT A MUSTANG TO BEAT PORSCHE — WHAT THE SOURCES SAY

scenes.text: We read Torque Café, Design News, Motor One, The Drive, AutoGuide and Wikipedia. We will tell you what Ford's executives said in their own words, what the lap times were, and where the sources disagree. We will also tell you what nobody has said. And we will show you why Porsche belongs in the story, even though no source puts it there as the target.
scenes.caption: SOURCES: TORQUE CAFÉ · DESIGN NEWS · MOTOR1 · THE DRIVE · AUTOGUIDE · WIKIPEDIA

scenes.text: The story begins with a race car, not a road car. Wikipedia says the Mustang GT3, developed by Ford Performance and Multimatic and based on the Dark Horse, was revealed in twenty twenty-three. It races in the IMSA SportsCar Championship and the FIA World Endurance Championship. Torque Café says the Mustang Dark Horse is the homologation model for the GT3 entry.
scenes.caption: MUSTANG GT3: FORD PERFORMANCE + MULTIMATIC, BASED ON DARK HORSE (WIKIPEDIA, TORQUE CAFÉ)

scenes.text: The race car took the Mustang back to Le Mans. Wikipedia says it raced there for the first time since nineteen ninety-seven, a gap of twenty-seven years. Proton Competition became the first customer team in the World Endurance Championship. Design News says Larry Holt, Multimatic's chief technology officer, supervised the GT3 programme, which finished third in the GT3 class at Le Mans.
scenes.caption: LE MANS RETURN AFTER 27 YEARS (WIKIPEDIA) · GT3 CLASS THIRD AT LE MANS (DESIGN NEWS)

scenes.text: Torque Café quotes Ford's chief executive, Jim Farley, at the launch of the seventh-generation Mustang in September twenty twenty-two: to go to Le Mans you need a road car. That is a single sentence, but it is the closest thing in our sources to a reason. The racing programme needed a road-going version, and the road car was the GTD. That is Farley's logic as quoted, not our interpretation.
scenes.caption: FARLEY, SEPT 2022: 'TO GO TO LE MANS YOU NEED A ROAD CAR' (TORQUE CAFÉ)

scenes.text: Torque Café also quotes Mark Rushbrook, who runs Ford Performance. He says: we don't want to make boring cars, and to have something like this, it is a passion product. And he says that as soon as Jim saw the GT3 there was no hesitation. So by Rushbrook's account, the decision was fast, and it was driven by enthusiasm as much as by any spreadsheet.
scenes.caption: RUSHBROOK: 'A PASSION PRODUCT' · 'AS SOON AS JIM SAW THE GT3 THERE WAS NO HESITATION' (TORQUE CAFÉ)

scenes.text: Executive chairman Bill Ford, quoted in the same article, says: we want to take everything to the apex and just do whatever is possible with that platform. He adds that the GTD is an expression of that. Notice what is missing from all three quotes. There is no rival named, no Porsche, no Ferrari, and no sales target. The stated motives are Le Mans, passion and the platform's limits.
scenes.caption: BILL FORD: 'TAKE EVERYTHING TO THE APEX' · 'GTD IS AN EXPRESSION OF THAT' (TORQUE CAFÉ)

scenes.text: Torque Café says Farley first hinted at the GTD in September twenty twenty-two. Its article is dated the twenty-sixth of June, twenty twenty-four, and quotes Rushbrook speaking at the GTD's public display at the twenty-four Hours of Le Mans. By our arithmetic, that is about twenty-one months from hint to article. Ford was using the race as its stage, which fits Farley's logic.
scenes.query: Ford Mustang GTD at Le Mans
scenes.caption: FIRST HINT SEPT 2022 → LE MANS ARTICLE JUNE 2024 ≈ 21 MONTHS (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Behind the badge is Multimatic. Torque Café describes it as a Canadian company that builds the Mustang GT3 and supplies the chassis for the Porsche nine sixty-three LMDh race car. It will also assemble the GTD, rather than Ford building it directly. This is the first place Porsche appears, and it is a surprise: the Mustang's builder also supplies a Porsche race car.
scenes.caption: MULTIMATIC: BUILDS MUSTANG GT3 · SUPPLIES PORSCHE 963 LMDh CHASSIS · ASSEMBLES THE GTD (TORQUE CAFÉ)

scenes.text: That does not mean Porsche helped build the Mustang. Nothing in our sources says so. It means the company that makes the Mustang GTD also works for a Porsche racing programme, which is a normal arrangement in motor racing, where specialist firms serve several teams. We mention it because it shows how connected these rivals are. The sources stop at the fact; the interpretation is ours.
scenes.caption: THE LINK IS THE SUPPLIER, NOT A COPY — NO SOURCE SAYS PORSCHE HELPED BUILD THE GTD

scenes.text: Design News adds that Multimatic built the GT3 and GTD and supplied the spool-valve shock absorbers. Larry Holt says the GTD has inboard suspension like prototype race cars, a dual-element rear wing with an active flap, and two ride heights. Torque Café says Ford claims the transaxle and carbon driveshaft give almost fifty-fifty weight distribution.
scenes.caption: INBOARD SUSPENSION · DUAL-ELEMENT ACTIVE WING · ~50/50 WEIGHT DISTRIBUTION (DESIGN NEWS, TORQUE CAFÉ)

scenes.text: The Drive puts it more bluntly: Multimatic massaged the chassis and suspension, and the car shares very little with a regular Mustang underneath. That is the outlet's description. It means the GTD is not a hot-rodded Mustang, it is a different car wearing the Mustang name. That helps explain the price, which The Drive gives as three hundred twenty-five thousand dollars plus.
scenes.caption: 'SHARES VERY LITTLE WITH A REGULAR MUSTANG UNDERNEATH' (THE DRIVE) · $325,000+

scenes.text: Now the promise. AutoGuide reported that at the debut in August twenty twenty-three, Farley promised a Nürburgring lap in under seven minutes. Design News quotes chief engineer Greg Goodall tying the engineering to the quest for a sub-seven-minute lap. We could only confirm the target from those two reports, not read the original speech, so we attribute it to them.
scenes.caption: SUB-7-MINUTE LAP TARGET (AUTOGUIDE, DESIGN NEWS — SPEECH NOT SEEN IN FULL)

scenes.text: The Nordschleife is the point of the whole project, and Ford chose it because it is the lap everyone compares. Seven minutes is four hundred twenty seconds. By our arithmetic, that is the line every GTD engineering decision was pointed at, according to Goodall. Anything slower would have been a failure of the promise, and anything faster a headline.
scenes.caption: 7:00 = 420 SECONDS (OUR ARITHMETIC) · THE TARGET ALL ENGINEERING POINTED AT (GOODALL, DESIGN NEWS)

scenes.text: The power figure moved too. Design News and Torque Café describe an engine of about eight hundred horsepower, a five point two litre supercharged V8. Ford's stated final output, according to Motor One and The Drive, is eight hundred fifteen, with six hundred sixty-four pound-feet of torque. So eight hundred was the earlier report, fifteen more was the final figure.
scenes.caption: ~800 HP (DESIGN NEWS, TORQUE CAFÉ, EARLIER) → 815 HP · 664 LB-FT (MOTOR1, THE DRIVE, WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: Design News makes one more point: the GTD can make more power than the GT3 race car, because it is not bound by racing rules. That is the key to the whole project. The race car must obey a class formula. The road car does not. So Ford could build a road car faster than its own race car on power, which is unusual, and it explains why the GTD exists at all.
scenes.query: Mustang GTD vs GT3 race car
scenes.caption: ROAD CAR CAN MAKE MORE POWER THAN THE RACE CAR — NO CLASS RULES (DESIGN NEWS)

scenes.text: Then the lap. Motor One reports that Dirk Müller of Multimatic Motorsports lapped the Nürburgring in six minutes, fifty-seven point six eight five seconds on the seventh of August, twenty twenty-four. Ford announced it on the tenth of December. By our arithmetic, that is one hundred twenty-five days later. The Drive agrees on the time and calls Müller a Le Mans winner.
scenes.caption: 6:57.685 · DIRK MÜLLER · RUN AUG 7, 2024 · ANNOUNCED DEC 10, 2024 (125 DAYS, OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, six fifty-seven point six eight five is four hundred seventeen point six eight five seconds. That is two point three one five seconds under the seven-minute line. It is not a large margin, which is why every tenth mattered, and why Farley's promise was risky. Two seconds on a lap of that length is a very thin cushion.
scenes.caption: 417.685 s vs 420 s TARGET → 2.315 s UNDER (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Motor One says the lap was the fastest by a North American production car and beat the Dodge Viper ACR by four point three seconds. The Drive says the previous American record was the Viper ACR at seven oh one point three oh, held for seven years, and calls the GTD roughly five seconds quicker. Our notes also list a Viper time of seven oh one point oh three. These do not agree with each other.
scenes.caption: VIPER ACR: 7:01.30 (THE DRIVE) · 7:01.03 (OUR EARLIER NOTES) · MARGIN: 4.3 s (MOTOR1) vs ~5 s (THE DRIVE)

scenes.text: Let us do the sums. Against seven oh one point three oh, the GTD is three point six one five seconds faster. Against seven oh one point oh three, it is three point three four five faster. Neither is four point three or five. So the three sources give three different margins, and we cannot tell you which is right. All agree on the direction: the GTD was quicker than any American production car before it.
scenes.caption: 7:01.30 → 3.615 s · 7:01.03 → 3.345 s · SOURCES SAY 4.3 s AND ~5 s — UNRESOLVED (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Motor One adds context. It says the GTD was one of six production sports cars worldwide to go under seven minutes, and the only American one. The Drive says only five production cars had gone faster. These agree, once you count the GTD itself. Motor One names the Mercedes-AMG One at six twenty-nine point oh nine as the overall production record, and the AMG GT Black Series at six forty-three point six one as the fastest front-engined car.
scenes.caption: ONE OF SIX UNDER 7:00 (MOTOR1) · 'ONLY FIVE FASTER' (THE DRIVE) · AMG ONE 6:29.09 · AMG GT BLACK SERIES 6:43.61

scenes.text: Farley's quote, in both Motor One and The Drive, is: we are proud to be the first American automaker with a car that can lap the Nürburgring in under seven minutes. He adds: we know there is much more time to find with Mustang GTD, we'll be back. Even at the moment of success, the chief executive was promising more. That is the clearest statement of intent in the sources.
scenes.caption: FARLEY: 'FIRST AMERICAN AUTOMAKER' UNDER SEVEN MINUTES · 'MUCH MORE TIME TO FIND… WE'LL BE BACK' (MOTOR1, THE DRIVE)

scenes.text: Now Porsche. The Drive's report on the lap does not mention Porsche at all. Motor One says the GTD's lap beat the Lamborghini Aventador SuperVeloce and the Ferrari 296 GTB and matched the Porsche 918 Spyder, with no times given. So at the moment of the record, the sources compare the GTD to Lamborghini, Ferrari and Porsche's hypercar, not to the Porsche 911 GT3.
scenes.caption: MOTOR1: BEAT AVENTADOR SUPERVELOCE AND FERRARI 296 GTB · MATCHED PORSCHE 918 SPYDER (NO TIMES GIVEN) · THE DRIVE: NO PORSCHE

scenes.text: The Porsche nine eleven G T three enters in our own comparison. Wikipedia's Porsche page lists a Nürburgring time of six fifty-five point three four for the nine ninety-two G T three. By our arithmetic, that is two point three four five seconds quicker than the Mustang's record lap of six fifty-seven point six eight five. So on those listed numbers, the first GTD lap did not beat that Porsche.
scenes.caption: 992 GT3: 6:55.34 (WIKIPEDIA) vs GTD 6:57.685 → GT3 FASTER BY 2.345 s (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: We need to be careful. We do not know whether those two times were set under the same conditions, tyres, or rules, and Wikipedia is not the same as an official timing. We are comparing listed numbers. But it is a useful correction to the title of this video. The GTD did not beat the Porsche nine eleven G T three on its first lap, on the numbers we found. It beat the Viper.
scenes.caption: CONDITIONS NOT VERIFIED — LISTED NUMBERS ONLY · FIRST GTD LAP DID NOT BEAT THE LISTED GT3 TIME

scenes.text: The later GTD laps are a different story. Wikipedia lists a GTD lap of six fifty-two point oh seven two in May twenty twenty-five. By our arithmetic, that is five point six one three seconds faster than the first lap, and three point two six eight seconds faster than the G T three's listed six fifty-five point three four. So by May twenty twenty-five, on listed numbers, the GTD was ahead.
scenes.caption: MAY 2025: 6:52.072 → 5.613 s FASTER THAN FIRST LAP · 3.268 s FASTER THAN LISTED GT3 (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: And the G T three R S? Wikipedia's Mustang page lists it at six forty-nine point three two eight, while Wikipedia's Porsche page lists six forty-four point eight four eight. Those are the same car and two different numbers, about four and a half seconds apart. By our arithmetic, four point four eight. We cannot tell you which is right. Either way, the R S is faster than the GTD's lap in May.
scenes.caption: GT3 RS: 6:49.328 (MUSTANG PAGE) vs 6:44.848 (PORSCHE PAGE) → 4.48 s APART (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The rival that the sources do treat as a threat is American. The Drive says the Corvette ZR1 was the only American car that could challenge the GTD's time, with one thousand sixty-four horsepower from a twin-turbo five point five litre V8, and likely much cheaper. It calls the comparison apples-to-oranges, because the GTD has no power or active aero limitations on its side.
scenes.caption: ZR1: 1,064 HP, TWIN-TURBO 5.5 L V8, 'ONLY AMERICAN CAR THAT COULD CHALLENGE' THE GTD (THE DRIVE)

scenes.text: Wikipedia lists the answer. In July twenty twenty-five, the Corvette ZR1 lapped the Nürburgring in six fifty point seven six three, and the ZR1X in six forty-nine point two seven five. By our arithmetic, the ZR1 was one point three oh nine seconds faster than the GTD's May lap, and the ZR1X two point seven nine seven. So the Mustang held the American record for only a matter of months.
scenes.caption: ZR1 6:50.763 · ZR1X 6:49.275 (JULY 2025, WIKIPEDIA) → 1.309 s AND 2.797 s FASTER THAN GTD'S MAY LAP (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Ford's reply, in Wikipedia's account, came on the seventeenth of April, twenty twenty-six: the GTD Competition, a pre-production car with magnesium wheels, dive planes, wheel aero discs and a modified wing, which lapped in six forty point eight three five. By our arithmetic, that is eight point four four seconds faster than the ZR1X's listed time and sixteen point eight five faster than the first GTD lap.
scenes.caption: GTD COMPETITION 6:40.835 (APR 17, 2026) → 8.44 s FASTER THAN ZR1X · 16.85 s FASTER THAN FIRST GTD LAP (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Farley said, we will be back. The sources show he was. Six minutes fifty-seven, then fifty-two, then forty. By our arithmetic, the lap time dropped by sixteen point eight five seconds in about twenty months, from August twenty twenty-four to April twenty twenty-six. Whatever Ford's motive, the race for the American record became a public contest between Ford and Chevrolet.
scenes.query: Ford vs Chevrolet at the Nürburgring
scenes.caption: 6:57.685 → 6:52.072 → 6:40.835 · −16.85 s IN ~20 MONTHS (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The GTD is not sold like a normal car. Torque Café says buyers must complete an application form stating their credentials, and that Ford uses the process to deter speculators from flipping cars for profit. It says the process opened in Europe after starting in the United States, and that Australian buyers can reportedly apply through the European process.
scenes.caption: APPLICATION TO DETER FLIPPERS · OPENED IN EUROPE AFTER THE US (TORQUE CAFÉ)

scenes.text: This is part of the story of why it exists. A halo car is not built for volume. Torque Café's description of a passion product, and the application process, fit a car meant to carry the brand rather than to sell in numbers. We have no production figure to confirm that. No source we found states how many GTDs Ford will build. That is a gap, and we will not fill it.
scenes.caption: PRODUCTION NUMBER: NOT STATED IN ANY SOURCE WE FOUND

scenes.text: The price shows the same logic. Motor One says the GTD officially starts at three hundred twenty-seven thousand, nine hundred sixty dollars with fees and tax, the most of any Mustang, ever. Wikipedia lists a top speed of two hundred two miles per hour. The Drive says the car shares very little with a regular Mustang underneath. Together those facts describe a flagship, not a sports coupe.
scenes.caption: $327,960 ALL-IN (MOTOR1) · 202 MPH (WIKIPEDIA) · 'SHARES VERY LITTLE WITH A REGULAR MUSTANG' (THE DRIVE)

scenes.text: There is also the question of what came after. Wikipedia says that in January twenty twenty-six, Ford produced a Dark Horse SC with the supercharged five point two litre V8 at seven hundred ninety-five horsepower and six hundred sixty pound-feet. By our arithmetic, that is twenty horsepower fewer than the GTD's eight hundred fifteen. The GTD's engine appears to have spread into the regular range.
scenes.caption: DARK HORSE SC: 795 HP / 660 LB-FT vs GTD 815 HP / 664 LB-FT → −20 HP (WIKIPEDIA, OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Let us line the laps up in seconds, so the pace of the contest is clear. By our arithmetic, the first GTD lap is four hundred seventeen point six eight five. The May lap is four hundred twelve point oh seven two. The ZR1 is four hundred ten point seven six three, the ZR1X four hundred nine point two seven five, and the GTD Competition four hundred point eight three five.
scenes.caption: GTD 417.685 · GTD (MAY 2025) 412.072 · ZR1 410.763 · ZR1X 409.275 · GTD COMPETITION 400.835 (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Measured against the seven-minute line of four hundred twenty seconds, by our arithmetic, the first lap beat it by two point three one five. The May lap beat it by seven point nine two eight. The ZR1 beat it by nine point two three seven, and the ZR1X by ten point seven two five. The Competition car beat it by nineteen point one six five. A promise kept by two seconds became a promise kept by nineteen.
scenes.caption: UNDER 7:00 BY: 2.315 s · 7.928 s · 9.237 s · 10.725 s · 19.165 s (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Horsepower tells a second story. The Drive gives the ZR1 one thousand sixty-four horsepower, and Ford's figure for the GTD is eight hundred fifteen. By our arithmetic, the Corvette has two hundred forty-nine more, or about thirty-one percent more than the Mustang. Yet in May twenty twenty-five the GTD was only about one point three seconds slower on the lap, so power is clearly not the only factor.
scenes.query: Corvette ZR1 vs Mustang GTD power
scenes.caption: ZR1 1,064 HP vs GTD 815 HP → +249 HP (+30.6%) · LAP GAP ONLY ~1.3 s (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The Drive offers its own explanation of why the comparison is awkward: the GTD, it says, has no power or active aero limitations. Design News says the Performance package adds active aerodynamics, and that in drag-reduction mode the rear flap flattens to cut drag. Holt says the front underwing opens two flaps to reduce downforce. So the GTD can change its shape, which a simple horsepower figure cannot capture.
scenes.caption: ACTIVE REAR FLAP + TWO FRONT UNDERWING FLAPS (HOLT, DESIGN NEWS) · 'NO ACTIVE AERO LIMITATIONS' (THE DRIVE)

scenes.text: There is a final disagreement worth showing, about when the GTD was introduced. Torque Café says Farley first hinted at it in September twenty twenty-two. AutoGuide, as we cited, places the debut in August twenty twenty-three. Wikipedia's text, as we read it, gives a different unveiling date in twenty twenty-two. We cannot reconcile these, so we use only the earliest hint and the later debut, and we do not claim a single unveiling date.
scenes.caption: HINT: SEPT 2022 (TORQUE CAFÉ) · DEBUT: AUG 2023 (AUTOGUIDE) · WIKIPEDIA DATE DIFFERS — NOT USED

scenes.text: One more voice. Torque Café says the GTD's rear dampers were developed by Multimatic, and Design News quotes Holt calling the transaxle a standard feature of race cars. Torque Café says the suspension lowers by forty millimetres at the track, and Holt gives the rear as thirty. These are small details, but they all come from race-car practice, as Holt describes it.
scenes.caption: MULTIMATIC DAMPERS · TRANSAXLE · TRACK LOWERING 40 MM FRONT (TORQUE CAFÉ), 30 MM REAR (HOLT)

scenes.text: The sources describe the GTD's parts. They do not say how Porsche's engineers regard them, or whether Porsche was ever the target. What we can say is that the car's builder, Multimatic, supplies a Porsche race car chassis, and that the lap-time rivalry in the sources is with Lamborghini, Ferrari and Chevrolet. The Porsche comparison is the viewer's, and ours, not Ford's.
scenes.caption: SOURCES' RIVALS: LAMBORGHINI, FERRARI, CHEVROLET

scenes.text: Now what we cannot tell you. No source we read says Ford built the GTD to beat Porsche. No source says what Ford's internal target was, beyond the seven-minute lap. No source gives production numbers. No source explains why a company known for trucks and affordable cars wanted a three hundred thousand dollar flagship. We have quotes about passion and Le Mans, and that is all.
scenes.caption: NOT IN ANY SOURCE: PORSCHE AS THE TARGET · INTERNAL GOALS · PRODUCTION NUMBERS · BUSINESS CASE
scenes.chapter: What the sources do not say

scenes.text: So the title of this video is a question, and the honest answer is in parts. Ford says it wanted a road car to go with its Le Mans race car. Its executives say they wanted to make something special, and they set a sub-seven-minute Nürburgring target and hit it. The Porsche in the title is our framing of a rivalry, not a Ford statement.
scenes.caption: THE ANSWER: LE MANS ROAD CAR + PASSION + A 7-MINUTE LAP. 'BEAT PORSCHE' IS OUR FRAMING, NOT FORD'S

scenes.text: What does the evidence support? That a race programme created a road car. That a Canadian specialist built it. That its engine, aero and suspension came from racing. That the lap time was a public promise, kept by two seconds. That rivals answered within months. Those are all sourced. The rest, including any claim about Porsche as a target, would be speculation, and we leave it out.
scenes.caption: SOURCED: RACE PROGRAMME → ROAD CAR · MULTIMATIC BUILD · RACE-DERIVED PARTS · KEPT PROMISE · RIVALS REPLIED

scenes.text: Was the GTD a Porsche beater or a Le Mans souvenir? Tell us in the comments, and if you have a sourced Nürburgring time that resolves any of the disagreements we showed, include the link. In the other videos of this series, we look at two secrets inside the Mustang GTD, compare it with the nine eleven G T three, and count what it costs to own. Our twenty twenty-seven Truck Buyer's Guide is linked below. Subscribe to Pickup Reality.
scenes.caption: SUBSCRIBE: PICKUP REALITY
